Messages.Author: Pierre
Messages.Body:
Right.

Finally back home after the European championship in Paris, somehow
recovered from massive drinking on the way back, a lot of conflicting
thoughts are still swirling in my head. The report part of this post
will be relatively short as i didn't do very well during the qualifier
and was absolutely abysmal during the EC proper :) Anyway here goes:

Travelling to Paris with the Legbiter family and Barny "Number 1"
Baker, we represented the English delegation at the EC. The trip in
itself was allright, tiring as can be expected, we managed to get a
game going on the ferry and learned how to play Munchkin, great fun :)
Arriving in the early hours of Saturday we jumped into the train to
Paris after some friendly negociations with the ticket office guy
(sarcasm), found our way through the Underground network of the French
capital and finally made it to Ostelen. Fast registration, well
organised and ready to handle a lot of players. We hanged out, meeting
some of the players, catching up with friends and acquaintances then
onto the Qualifier.

Against my better judgment, i played (again) my Tzimisce deck that i
played both at GenCon and the Qualifier in Watford. I wanted to play
my Courier deck for comedy value as i was already qualified. But at
the last minute, i realised that i had about three Jyhad cards in the
deck and no time left to de-sleeve another deck to sleeve this
one....so i played the Tzimisce, didn't really mind as i have reached
some kind of symbiosis with the deck :)

A lot of things happened during the Qualifier, many unrelated to the
game itself. An accumulation of little things during the first rounds
drastically changed my mood to its darkest levels in years. The
constant presence and interference of the judge assigned to the table
made for a really stressful game, of everything being to tap my cards
to, and i quote "exactly 90 degrees" while i've tapped cards since the
early days of MTG to about 45 :) An extra effort of 45 degrees! i
don't think he realised what he was asking :) And before any of you
say it's nothing, it's just an example among many. Still i complied.
With the referees hovering around the tables, checking hands and, i
believe, enforcing the rules as they were told to do so, games were
considerably lengthened in some cases and, knowing that my deck has a
tendency to time out, i felt worried but still pretty good about the
whole tournament and being part of such an event. Since i managed to
get 3VPs in the first round and seeing the general lack of a serious
threat to my Fiends, i quite fancied my chances at reaching the final.
Had to do my decklist detween the rounds and as i was doing so, some
bloke showed up and told me that i shouldn't be allowed to do without
judge supervision, since i could have been cheating....sigh...
Ignoring him, and thinking no more of it, i went on to play the second
round. Preyed on by a weenie Presence vote deck, i felt pretty
confident i could stop him in his tracks which i did, and although i
took some early damage, once tooled up with Winthrop and Eternal
Vigilance, my friend Meshenka went on slaugthering the precious small
vamps of my predator. A lot of votes were attempted, and since all the
players had some votes, the table talks were numerous, lengthy and
heated, which made for a great game, if a bit frustrating for the
French players with a limited ability in English. However during the
game, Stephane (prince of Paris) came to me to talk about James
"Legbiter" McClellan and his closeness to a game loss due to extreme
agitation and attitude toward the judge. Those of you who know James
would have been equally surprised to hear that. I could indeed hear
some commotion from the other side of the room and thought it was
pretty serious stuff. That added to my perception that there was
something wrong in the judges' general attitude and way of handling
the players. James came to talk shortly after being ousted and voiced
his total outrage at everything, coming close to torching the place
down in memory of centuries of hostilities between French and English,
but being Scottish, he couldn't really do that, could he? Lucky for
Ostelen :) Anyway i finished the round with 0 VP, for a total of 3VPs
so far. The performance was alright so i do not believe my feelings
about the events could have been clouded by my score (as opposed to
James maybe). Between the rounds, i recall getting rather angry at
anything and everything, seriously considering dropping out of the
tournament, and giving up on the game as well. I know more than a few
would have happily taken that box of trades of my hands :) Still
prompted by Barny, i went outside to get some fresh air and cool
off....did me well, and decided not to give the adversity the
satisfaction....
Third round was pretty fun, my thanks to my predator for playing a
really cool deck (Gangrel daring/slow body/rapid healing) and being a
great chap :) Cheers man! you did a lot of damage before dying still
Anyway i only managed to scape one extra VP before being sneak/bled
for my remaining pool. No final for me :( still a respectable total of
4 VPs.

Hearing that Anklebiter played his third round against 4 other French
who did not bother talking in English the whole made my blood boil one
more time, Michael knew he should have called the judge but according
to him, he couldn't prove anything after the facts. Think about it,
you call the judge and say that the other players were saying
something in French but you didn't know what it was and even if it was
relevant to the game; for all he knew they could have been talking
about what they had for lunch :) Barny made it into the final and i
decided to watch out for a repeat of that and provide the occasional
translation. The final proceeded under the watchful eye of some
judges. Some suspicious play was the downfall of Barny....so we left
to meet up with the Legbiters and our host Reyda....only for me
discuss outside with Philippe, Kamel and some others and to get into a
real argument about everything that happened so far, how i was
disguted with the tournament in general and judges' lack of
discernment in particular, the way it felt very much like a MTG
tournament, etc...Still when reading this i hope they will remember
that i did acknowledge the effort and time they all put in the
organisation, the way a lot of players voiced their concerns about
enforcing the VEKN rules back in July. Anyway after it appears that i
could have stay up and argue all night in front of Ostelen, i was
dragged away under the promise of beer and food and a game of Munchkin
(deciding argument). Before leaving, Kamel did tell me the points i
raised where going to be discussed during a judges meeting the next
morning.
Some beer and nice food after, at Reyda's flat, cool 6 players
Munchkin game which finished James off. Time for some sleep....

Next day, the European Championship! I decided to go with a weenie
Potence deck and, thanks to the previous day, already in Jack-booted
Thug mode. I suppose i'd be lying if i'd say i just went for the fun.
Of course i intended to win but having a great time was the primary
objective. I can say right now that i must have had the best time of
my VTES life, despite the fact that my deck was 100% untested.... The
deck appeared to be a very good metagame choice as many many players
relied solely on majesty and/or obedience for combat defence....far
from enough to keep my rampaging hordes away from long :)

First round went fairly ok, being bled for 12 by my giovanni predator
plus some deflected bleeds did hamper my development so i was pushed
in the ropes from the start. I had to calm him down or die, rushed,
burned Andrea with a topdecked Burning Wrath and disarmed Isabel. He
died shortly after and i followed after holding on for a good
while....0 VP

Second round, four vote decks and myself...not the best as my only
hope of influencing the table relied on threatening the other players'
vamps with extreme prejudice and loss of limb, and it did work :)
After passing a non-agression pact with my predator, i never took a
damage from a KRC or ConAg, the voters usually took the extra point
themselves :) I had my prey quite low, as was my grand prey...about
4-5 minions, gearing up for the killing blow when my pred called a
restructure....him killing my prey, his pred killing my grand prey (to
insure his votes), leaving me with squat...I did persuade the
remaining players to withdraw as the time limit approached, winning me
a VP.
Each vote was the subject of lengthy discussions, short- and long-term
alliances and grudges....all the table talk was conducted in English
and everything was fine until one of the judge decide to meddle.
Despite having the poorest English of the lot, the judge kept
interfering with the table talks and vote counting. I suppose he
thought he was helping but honestly he wasn't so i politely asked him
to leave and let us sort things out between adults, which he did :) No
threat necessary :)
Play went on smoothly and friendly, despite the tension and stake of
the game...until another judge decided it was time to pester us again.
All hell went loose when i decided to play an Ambush on Prince Tim of
my current prey (Guillaume?) when Ruben (the infamous) begged me to
rush Sir Walter Nash so that he could Majesty, Untap and bounce some
of his pred's bleeds....so i said ok i'll take that back, let me think
about it. This prompted an intervention from the judge telling me that
i wasn't allowed to show my cards to other players....well duh, i knew
that....i was gonna play the card but chose to reconsider the
situation with the new info i had...well the Jack-booted Thug mode
struck and i proceeded to tell him that if i had really wanted to
reveal some or all of my cards, i could have drop my hand "by
mistake", etc...and told him to leave us alone to play, he threatened
me with a warning, i didn't back down, took my warning for
that...honestly didn't even remember that warnings existed in
VTES....couldn't care less about it anyway. When all three players
remaining decided to withdraw, the judge decided to make us go through
the motion of discarding our whole crypt evenso we had about 10-15
minutes left, spiteful move, lack of discernment?
Actually at the end of the round i felt pretty happy, one VP and one
warning, the Cosmic Balance and all ;) You might think that my
decision to get rid off the judge was selfish but i did ask the other
players and all of them were sick and tired of the unwanted presence.

Third round was again very enjoyable, got the chance to play against
Reyda and Francois, made them regret their hospitality ;) As well on
the table, Belgian Jeroen and American Ben....another great game,
great decks all around, lots of trash talking and fighting
talks...mainly backed up by Ben who only lost Ozmo in all my
cross-table actions. Reyda tried to kill me at some point (evenso i
was holding off him from the start, him being sneak/bled by Ben) and
would have done it if Francois hadn't decided to Life Boon me, a move
that proved fatal to him in the end...Jeroen's deck would have swept
if i hadn't managed to cut his deck so all his progenies and embraces
were in the second half of his deck ;) He did keep me alive against
Ben's Malks by calling three ConsagBoon on my two Panders :) In the
end, we three timed out, bringing my grand total of VP for the EC to a
mighty 1.5 :) That will teach me to bring an untested deck to such a
major event...
The final wasn't for me...would have loved to watch it but i had to
sort out travel arrangements for Barny and myself....running around
for options and solutions :) Thanks to Francois, everything was sorted
out. Barny bit the dust in the final after a more than valiant
struggle....again congrats to the winner, i hope you'll defend your
title next year...the Thug will be after revenge :)...nah just
kidding...or am i?

Prizes were pretty cool, we all grabbed our stuff and headed off to a
cafe for a well deserved Guiness. Left for Pigalle (Paris red light
district) to grab some food and drinks at Denis' flat, oh and some
more cards, planting beans is cool :) Crashed at Francois' place for
the night before he generously offered to drive us all the way to Le
Havre (i hope the return was fine man), for us to take the afternoon
ferry to finally head back to English soil....at last :) That
concludes our EC experience, the rest is a tad blurry and fragmented
as much drinking occured on the way back.

Time for the props and slops:
Props:
-to Reyda and Francois, for their hospitality and generosity, it will
not be forgotten or unrewarded when you decide to come over here for
some beers and cards
-to the organising team of the EC, for a very smooth tournament
despite the number of players
-to the judges for handling all questions asked with alacrity.
-to Ostelen for a great venue
-to all the people i met and were polite enough to let ramble on,
especially Gines, Ruben (the infamous), Roberto and many other, hope
to see you all next time.
-to Barny for telling to chill out when i was ready to flip tables and
inflict bodily harm :)
-to the Jack-booted Thug mode
-to the diversity of decks at the EC, some great concept decks and
daring metagame choices
-to the Spanish delegation for filming all the decks and the final, i
hope those CDs will be ready to be shipped soon guys, i can hardly
wait :)
-to all the people who took pictures during both days, i hope you'll
find the time to upload everything on some websites
-to the winner of the EC with a very cool Derange deck.

Slops:
-to Barny for not winning the EC, after all the trouble i went through
to find a way for us to travel back :)
-to the judges for forgetting to wear the velvet glove over the iron
fist, but i appreciated the improvment from Saturday to Sunday, i hope
my rant of the evening had something to do with it
-to me for bringing an untested deck to the EC
-to the amount of S/B decks at the Qualifier, but then again
everybody's free to play what they want
-to the judges (2) for disqualifying players for tardiness, that was a
bit excessive, wasn't it?
-to me again for having an obscene trading box, and disappointing many
traders after my many War Ghouls, sorry guys ;)

That's it for me, i hope i didn't offend too many ppl :) Thanks for
reading all the way down to the end :P
P. Tzimisce Jack-Booted Thug

was judged is positive. Especially from people who had to suffer from my
judgments, for example David, about the VP split who reacted in a very
positive way despite being screwed up, which I much appreciated-the positive
way i mean, not the screwing up :), or a player from Hungary (sorry, no name
available again), who played Brujah with much roleplay, real cool to watch,
and who displayed the best fair play I've ever seen.

Not disqualify AFAIK. But not allowing them to participate in a round, yes.
At any rate, it is granted IMHO this is still excessive, but:
-on saturday the place players had to leave by 9:30-10PM because of a
Magic:tG tourney lasting for the night.so we were tight on schedule.
Especially when laptop computers decide to lose their +1 bleed and decide to
f*** up instead, just when organizers thought they had their fill of
problems.

The worst situation in that respect was the final of the 1st day, as one of
the finalist wasn't here when we asked for him over the
loudspeaker/mic/whatever. After waiting, we had to settle on the 6th player
(not here), the 7th (same IIRC) and finally 8th. After the "new" finalists
had determined the seating order, shuffled their decks and prepared their
counters, the 3rd finalist showed up. We had either to prevent him or the
8th finalist from playing...Real tough decision to make since one player had
to suffer from the judgment. We let the 8th player play the final, as we
thought that people weren't that interested in that final since it wouldn't
change the "qualified" state at all, and so maybe left. It was getting late
and we had no way of knowing if the 3rd player was coming at all.

-on sunday we were also tight on schedule. don't think there were any
problems on sunday, though.

Stone

VEKN rules without considering opinions of the other players at the

all-dancing God of any judge) make for a better game? Do you really
enjoy being considered a cheater by default?

circumstances might entail an adapted application of the rules? You
also admit that other things might have influenced judges' decisions,
is it really to much to ask that the same might be true for players
and that judges are not omniscient creatures hence do not take
precedence over the players involved in the game?

EC are currently bones of contention and definately agree that simple
solutions seem out of range for now. Conflicting playstyles and
regional differences did make for even a stronger clash but, don't get
me wrong, the EC was a success and i do not regret the expense in
retrospect. Having discussed with some of the organisers on Saturday
evening, it appears that they experienced rotten play in Paris and in
other places, and decided to apply VEKN rules to the letter to prevent
that, which i understand. But assuming that a player is fundamentally
bad does not appear as really sane for the game we all know and love,
doesn't the saying go something like innocent until proven guilty.

detailled and complete will never cover all the potential problems; a
devious mind will always find holes and ways to abuse the system to
its own advantage. I'm not naive enough to believe that every one is
good natured and we all live in Happyhappy Land, let's not forget that
vigilance remains the price of freedom, too little or too much and
freedom disappears to chaos or facism....On this very philosophical
ending, i bid you farewell.

players, unsportsmanlike players, and cheaters. Rules are needed to protect
the players. Rules have 2 edges however, and their rigid enforcement screw
up players who lost their concentration for a second.

abusing more flexible interpretation of the rules. There are countless
situations in which a player would give a significant advantage when allowed
to take back his card into hand, not re-shuffling the deck after having put
back a card drawn during a referendum, discarding when the prey has played
his mater card, etc.

It's not all black and white. You can think of it as a lesser evil, if you
want.
If everyone was sportsmanlike, fair play, and willing to have fun on top
priority, rigid enforcement of the rules is not needed. This is not the
case. Either filter players or be strict with the rules, and you have the
lesser evil.

tourney. Then you get to meet cheaters/unsportsmanlike jerks/lawyers taking

Judges are not omniscient and this holds true for the people who made the
rules of VtES, as well of the tournament rules. Nobody's perfect, but still
rules are needed and judges are needed, even if they're not perfect.

> bad does not appear as really sane for the game we all know and love,

> Besides, and MTG has proved it, the tournament rules, no matter how
> detailled and complete will never cover all the potential problems; a
> devious mind will always find holes and ways to abuse the system to

There will be always pros and cons to each style of judging. A devious
player will have a much, much harder time to get away with abuses, if the
rules are enforced in an unambiguous way. Players having different playstyle
and different cultures can acknowledge a uniform way of handling situations.
These are the pros. The cons are more pressure since players must avoid the
little mistakes allowed during friendly games, a possibly less cheerful
atmosphere. I've seen people smiling during games, when collecting prizes
(and everyone had at least 3 boosters), when saying goodbye. I haven't seen
burned cars outside Ostelen, but you already said the EC was a success so I
stop straying into rambling. My point is that IMO people can adapt
themselves and cope with the pressure of tournament play, while at the same
time still having a good time.

Stone

Specifically, the rules state that you must present your deck to your predator for
additional randomizing. However, they also allow for any opponent to request the
judge to randomize the deck further, though it's his decision whether he thinks it
should be done or not.

As for the judge taking it upon himself to grab a player's deck and shuffle it, the
rules clearly provide for that in a different section (2.5) which requires the judge
to "take action to resolve any rules infraction (whether a violation of the V:EKN
Tournament Rules or the game rules) they notice or that is brought to their attention."
Since insufficient randomization of a deck is against tournament rules, the judge is
clearly within his prerogative to do this if he felt a player hadn't adequately shuffled.

By the way, why should it even matter? If the deck was randomized before, it just
gets randomized some more. That's harmless enough. As long as this judge isn't
constantly wasting everyone's time with unnecessary play stoppages for this kind of
thing.

Fred

> gets randomized some more. That's harmless enough. As long as this judge isn't
> constantly wasting everyone's time with unnecessary play stoppages for this kind of
> thing.

From what other people have said, they don't like the tone that this sets.

"Hi player, I've just randomised your deck because I don't think it
is. Ergo, I think you were cheating."

Whether true or not, this is the tone it sets for many players where
Jyhad has been a game that is played based on trust, much of the time.

If it was randomised already, there was no need for it to be done,
which could in a number of situations significantly slow the game down
- because the player cannot draw cards and continue their turn if it
was from, say, searching with Al's Army Apparatus (or whatever, there
are many examples).

--

>

> Jyhad has been a game that is played based on trust, much of the time.

All right, I can see your point. I guess it all depends on what the player in question
did which caused the judge to do what he did. If the player really did a decent job of
shuffling and no one can figure out what the judge is thinking (or the judge seems to be
carrying some sort of grudge for the player), then you're right. I've just seen a lot
of players who do half-assed things when shuffling their decks: deliberately prearranging
cards before shuffling, pulling out decks they want us to assume are already shuffled and
just cutting them a couple of times (I'm sure the vast majority of the time they _were_
preshuffled and nothing is going on but I don't like being expected to trust them on that
point), or just plain doing a lousy job of shuffling. So I find it easy to imagine
someone doesn't want to accept the feedback that they need to do a better job. If the
judge was off the wall one time, who cares? Just make sure you look like you're _really_
shuffling in the future.

Fred

BTW, this is my argument against cutting someone's deck. If the person isn't
cheating, what possible benefit is there to cutting a deck? The disadvantage
is clearly one of wasting time. If I go first in V:TES, I have to sit and wait
for the last player to shuffle and be cut rather than just start.

Yet, for some reason, people cut decks all the time. Mindless tradition, I
guess.

>From what other people have said, they don't like the tone that this sets.

I recall a store MtG tourney where one player was caught with two
sideboards. He said it was an accident and protested loudly. The
reality was that he was a cheater as he showed in incidents after
that. He sounded innocent until you looked further.

>"Hi player, I've just randomised your deck because I don't think it
>is. Ergo, I think you were cheating."

The "Ergo . . ." doesn't automatically follow.

>Whether true or not, this is the tone it sets for many players where
>Jyhad has been a game that is played based on trust, much of the time.

Can we not trust people to shuffle adequately? Sometimes, it
appears that answer is no.

>If it was randomised already, there was no need for it to be done,
>which could in a number of situations significantly slow the game down
>- because the player cannot draw cards and continue their turn if it
>was from, say, searching with Al's Army Apparatus (or whatever, there
>are many examples).

If the deck is exposed, then it is no longer sufficiently
randomized.
